newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Phillips says ready to go on Australia LNG.
newsitem.headline: Phillips says ready to go on Australia LNG.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co said on Monday it was ready to proceed with its proposed liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in the Northern Territory using gas from the offshore Bayu-Undan field in the Australia/Indonesia Zone of Cooperation.
"Phillips is ready to proceed with this project today," Eric Wiszneauckas, Timor Sea project manager for Phillips said in a paper delivered to an energy conference in Darwin.
"Upon selection of the onshore LNG plant project, Phillips plans to initiate immediate efforts to secure the LNG market for this plant."
Phillips differs with its joint venture partner, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, over location of an LNG processing plant.
Phillips wants to the plant to be located onshore in Darwin utilising proven in-house technology but BHP favours an offshore facility.
A proposed Royal Dutch/Shell -Woodside Petroleum Ltd venture also calls for an onshore LNG plant in Darwin.

Bayu-Undan, which is estimated to contain proven and probable reserves of 1.3 trillion cubic feet of gas and about 400 million barrels of hydrocarbon liquids, will require initial expenditure of more than A$1 billion on facilities to strip condensate and liquefied petroleum gas from reserves, for first producion in 1998.
BHP last month said it hoped for a decision on the project, including the LNG plant, estimated to cost up to A$4.0 billion, "as soon as possible."
